declarations.name: Becoming.LineOnAStock.takes_the_whole
declarations.lean_statement:
theorem takes_the_whole [DecidablePred S] (one : ∀ u, S u → need u = m) (pos : 0 < m)
    (grows : ∀ u, S u → use u < lineTake S use (kids u)) (outside : ∀ u, ¬ S u → m ≤ need u)
    (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving) (keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi)
    {w : List U} {x : Nat} (high : x ≤ hi) {u₀ : U} (mem : u₀ ∈ w) (line : S u₀) :
    ∃ n, n ≤ hi + 1 ∧
      (∀ j, j < n → m ≤ (course need kids giving use (w, x) j).2) ∧
      (course need kids giving use (w, x) n).2 < m ∧
      «迭» (net need kids giving use) n (w, x) (course need kids giving use (w, x) n) ∧
      (∀ v, ¬ net need kids giving use (course need kids giving use (w, x) n) v) ∧
      ((∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → S v → S u) →
        strip (fun v => ¬ S v) (course need kids giving use (w, x) n).1 =
          strip (fun v => ¬ S v) (generation kids n w))
declarations.told_in_words: The item's law. For any decidable S. Premises: every unit of S needs m (one); 0 < m (pos); each unit of S has kids of S that together take more than it (grows); every unit not of S needs at least m (outside); nothing is given from nothing (nothing); the step under no take keeps every level up to hi within hi (keeps); the start level is at most hi (high); a unit of S is in the start way (mem, line). Conclusion: there is a step n ≤ hi + 1 such that the level is at least m at every step before n and below m at n; the net from (w, x) reaches the course's configuration at step n in n steps; that configuration conditions nothing (no need is met there, so the net has ended); and, where no unit outside S leaves a unit of S (closure, asked by this last conjunct only, as an implication inside the conclusion), the way there stripped of the units not of S is the n-th generation of w so stripped. Rests on falls_below (which rests on rise, lineCount_pos, lineTake_le_taken, first_of_decided and the new rising_floor_takes_all), Law.stepWhile_steps_iff, Law.stepWhile_none_iff, and line_way for the last conjunct. Proof: 10 lines.

declarations.name: Becoming.LineOnAStock.falls_below
declarations.lean_statement:
theorem falls_below [DecidablePred S] (grows : ∀ u, S u → use u < lineTake S use (kids u))
    (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving) (keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi)
    (pos : 0 < m) {s : List U × Nat} (high : s.2 ≤ hi)
    (below : ∀ j u, u ∈ (course need kids giving use s j).1 → S u → need u ≤ m)
    {u₀ : U} (mem : u₀ ∈ s.1) (line : S u₀) :
    ∃ n, n ≤ hi + 1 ∧ (∀ j, j < n → m ≤ (course need kids giving use s j).2) ∧
      (course need kids giving use s n).2 < m ∧
      ∀ j, j ≤ n → ∃ u, u ∈ (course need kids giving use s j).1 ∧ S u
declarations.told_in_words: The lemma that carries the law, and more general than it. For any decidable S, with no closure asked and nothing asked of the units not of S. Premises: each unit of S has kids of S that together take more than it (grows); nothing given from nothing; the step under no take keeps every level up to hi within hi; 0 < m; start level at most hi; every unit of S in a way of the course needs at most m (below; 'at most', not 'exactly'); a unit of S is in the start way. Conclusion: there is a step n ≤ hi + 1 at which the level is below m, the level at least m at every step before n, and a unit of S in the way at every step up to n. Argument: were the level at least m up to step hi + 1, the units of S would be met and one of them present at each step (line_while), so what S takes would rise at each step (rise, lineCount_pos); what the way takes is at least that; so the level at hi + 1 would be nothing (rising_floor_takes_all), below m. Proof: 23 lines.

declarations.name: Becoming.TurningInTime.rising_floor_takes_all
declarations.lean_statement:
theorem rising_floor_takes_all {W : Type u} {next : W → W} {level take q : W → Nat}
    {giving : Nat → Nat} {hi : Nat} (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving)
    (keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi)
    (steps : ∀ t, level (next t) = RegimeMargin.step giving (take t) (level t))
    (floor : ∀ t, q t ≤ take t) {s : W} (high : level s ≤ hi)
    (rises : ∀ j, j < hi → q (Law.orbit next s j) < q (Law.orbit next s (j + 1))) :
    level (Law.orbit next s (hi + 1)) = 0
declarations.told_in_words: New general lemma, needed because TurningInTime.rising_takes_all asks that the take itself rise. On the orbit of any next from s, read by a level, a take and a quantity q. Premises: nothing given from nothing; the step under no take keeps every level up to hi within hi; at every configuration the level after a step is RegimeMargin.step giving under the take (steps); q is at most the take at every configuration (floor); the start's level is at most hi; q rises strictly at each of the first hi steps of the orbit (rises). Conclusion: the level at step hi + 1 is nothing. The take may fall; only q must rise. By kept_within step by step, rises_from, and the last three lines of rising_takes_all's own proof. Proof: 9 lines.

declarations.name: Becoming.TurningInTime.rising_takes_all_as_case
declarations.lean_statement:
theorem rising_takes_all_as_case {W : Type u} {alone : W → W} {giving : Nat → Nat} {use : W → Nat}
    {hi : Nat} (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving) (keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi)
    {w : W} {x : Nat} (high : x ≤ hi)
    (rises : ∀ j, j < hi → use (Law.orbit alone w j) < use (Law.orbit alone w (j + 1))) :
    (Law.orbit (asItWas alone (fun w x => RegimeMargin.step giving (use w) x)) (w, x) (hi + 1)).2 = 0
declarations.told_in_words: The statement of TurningInTime.rising_takes_all, word for word, proved from rising_floor_takes_all with the quantity q the use itself, on the course as it was (asItWas_way carries the rise from alone's orbit). The private takes_at_hi is not used. Proof: 8 lines (the original: 7, plus the private takes_at_hi, which rising_meets_level still needs). So no line falls here; what changes is that the arithmetic is told once.

declarations.name: Becoming.LineOnAStock.line_kid / level_within / line_while (helpers of falls_below)
declarations.told_in_words: line_kid: a unit of S whose kids of S together take more than it has a kid of S (total_pos). level_within: with the step under no take keeping every level up to hi within hi, from a level at most hi every level of the course is at most hi (kept_within, step by step). line_while: with grows, every unit of S on the course needing at most m, and a unit of S in the start way, if the level is at least m at every step before n then a unit of S is in the way at every step up to n. Proofs: 4, 2 and 6 lines. line_kid and line_while are the one argument here that the home module does not already have in some form (ends_high asks at each step whether a unit of S is left instead).

declarations.name: Becoming.LineOnAStock.line_way (with strip_allKids, line_after_met)
declarations.lean_statement:
theorem strip_allKids {Z : U → Prop} [DecidablePred Z] (inZ : ∀ u v, Z u → v ∈ kids u → Z v)
    (w : List U) : strip Z (allKids kids (strip Z w)) = strip Z (allKids kids w)

theorem line_after_met [DecidablePred S] (closed : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → S v → S u) {x : Nat} :
    ∀ {w : List U}, (∀ u, u ∈ w → S u → need u ≤ x) →
      strip (fun v => ¬ S v) (after need kids w x) = strip (fun v => ¬ S v) (allKids kids w)

theorem line_way [DecidablePred S] (closed : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → S v → S u) {w : List U} {x : Nat} :
    ∀ n, (∀ j, j < n → ∀ u, u ∈ (course need kids giving use (w, x) j).1 → S u →
        need u ≤ (course need kids giving use (w, x) j).2) →
      strip (fun v => ¬ S v) (course need kids giving use (w, x) n).1 =
        strip (fun v => ¬ S v) (generation kids n w)
declarations.told_in_words: What can be had of one_need_ends' last conjunct. line_way: for a line S (closed: no unit outside it leaves a unit of it), under any need, giving and use, from any start: where at every step before n every unit of S in the way has its need met, the way at step n stripped of the units not of S is the n-th generation of the start way so stripped. Nothing is asked of the units not of S. It uses the home module's own strip, at the predicate 'not of S'. strip_allKids is strip_after at a need of nothing; line_after_met is the one-step form. Proofs: 5, 16 and 8 lines. way_while_met is the like statement for the whole way; I did not derive one from the other.

declarations.name: Becoming.LineOnAStock.line_gone_within
declarations.lean_statement:
theorem line_gone_within [DecidablePred S] (closed : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → S v → S u)
    (one : ∀ u, S u → need u = m) (pos : 0 < m)
    (grows : ∀ u, S u → use u < lineTake S use (kids u))
    (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving) (keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving 0 hi)
    {w : List U} {x : Nat} (high : x ≤ hi) :
    ∃ n, n ≤ hi + 2 ∧
      ∀ k, n ≤ k → ∀ u, u ∈ (course need kids giving use (w, x) k).1 → ¬ S u
declarations.told_in_words: The other end of the same relation, not asked for: what holds without the premise on the other units. For a closed line S of one need m, 0 < m, grows, nothing given from nothing, the step under no take keeping every level up to hi within hi, start at most hi; nothing asked of the units not of S and no unit of S need be in the start way. Conclusion: there is a step n ≤ hi + 2 from which no unit of S is in the way. By falls_below and gone_after (gone_from when no unit of S is at the start). line_ends states no such step and asks, in place of one need, positive needs and that every kid of a unit of S need no more than it; neither law's premises contain the other's. Whether the net ends is not concluded; on OutsideNeedsLess it does not. Proof: 7 lines.

impl.differs_from_asked:
The statement holds, and a little more than was asked.

1. Closure is not needed for the ending. `takes_the_whole` takes any decidable S. "No unit outside S leaves a unit of S" appears only as the hypothesis of the last conjunct, inside the conclusion.

2. The form of one_need_ends, and what cannot be had. Three of its four parts are had: a step at most hi + 1, the net reaching a configuration in that many steps, and that configuration conditioning nothing. The configuration is named (the course's at step n) instead of existentially bound, which is stronger. Two conjuncts are added: the level is at least m at every step before n, and below m at n. The fourth part, `t.1 = generation kids m w`, cannot be had: a unit outside the line that needs more than m can be unmet at a level that still meets m, and drops out. `OutsideNeedsMore.way_not_generation` proves this on a world where every premise holds. What is had instead, for a closed line: the way there stripped of the units not of the line is the generation so stripped (`line_way`).

3. The law rests on a more general lemma, `falls_below`: units of S need at most m (not exactly m), nothing is asked of the other units, no closure. It gives the step at most hi + 1 at which the level is below m. With it come two things not asked for: `line_gone_within` (a closed one-need line is gone within hi + 2 steps whatever else is in the way, which is what world C shows from the other end), and `ends_all` restated without `ends_high`.

4. `TurningInTime.rising_takes_all` could not carry the proof as it stands, so the module adds `rising_floor_takes_all` (a take that is at least a rising quantity) and restates `rising_takes_all` as its case.

Asked item 3, how thin the law is: thin. `takes_the_whole`'s proof is 10 lines. Two of them are the law's own content: below m no need is met because every need is at least m, the only place `outside` enters. The rest is `falls_below` and the two `Law.stepWhile` lemmas. `falls_below` (23 lines) is carried by the existing `rise`, `lineCount_pos`, `lineTake_le_taken`, `first_of_decided`, `TurningInTime.kept_within` and `TurningInTime.rises_from`. The only argument the home modules do not already have in some form is that a unit of the line stays in the way while the line is met (`line_kid` and `line_while`, 10 proof lines). `rising_floor_takes_all` (9 lines) is the arithmetic of `rising_takes_all` and `ends_high` said a third time, in the one form that covers all three.
impl.old_proofs_that_become_cases:
Measured in Lean lines, statements and proofs, docstrings not counted. Each restatement is proved in the scratch module under a new name.

- `LineOnAStock.one_need_ends` becomes the case S := fun _ => True of `takes_the_whole` (`one_need_ends_as_case`). Proof 16 lines before, 10 after; the 5-line statement is unchanged. It would no longer go through `need_unmet`, so its docstring's sentence that it rests on `TurningInTime.rising_takes_all` would change to `rising_floor_takes_all`. `need_unmet` stays; `falls_to_unmet` uses it. No other module uses `one_need_ends`.
- `LineOnAStock.ends_high` would go, and `ends_all` rests on `falls_below` instead (`ends_all_as_case`), so `line_ends` and `way_ends` follow unchanged. Before: `ends_high` 7 + 30 and `ends_all` 5 + 6, 48 lines, plus `ends_high`'s 12-line docstring. After: `below_along` 3 + 2 and `ends_all` 5 + 12, 22 lines. `ends_high` is used nowhere else.
- `TurningInTime.rising_takes_all` becomes the case "the quantity is the take" of `rising_floor_takes_all` (`rising_takes_all_as_case`). Proof 7 lines before, 8 after. The private `takes_at_hi` stays, because `rising_meets_level` uses it. No line falls here.

read.telling_that_is_safe: Take a flow on a web (whole-number levels; at each step some formations take part, taking from and giving to conditions), one condition c, a number m and a step T. Suppose that at every step from T on the level of c after the step, with what was taken from it, is its level before with what was given to it; that whatever takes part and gives to c is supported there (each condition it then depends on stands at least at its need); and that whatever takes part and gives to c depends on c at a need of at least m; and suppose that at T the level of c is below m. Then at every step from T on the level of c is below m and nothing is given to c, and it is not the case that something is taken from c at arbitrarily late steps; read on the family of c alone, over any N steps from T all that is taken is at most the level at T, and fewer than m of those steps take anything. No last step of taking is exhibited: what is proved is that taking does not recur without end, and that it is refuted that there is no step from which on nothing is taken. The law is of taking, not of arising: in a worked model with every premise holding, a formation that depends on c at a lower need and takes nothing is inactive and then active at arbitrarily late steps, its activity being set so and not read off its support; and for each of balance, the gate at need m, the level below m, only active formations giving, and activity needing support (the last two together give supported givers), a worked model has that one failing, the others holding, and something taken at every step. It is proved in Lean with an empty axiom report in a scratch module not on main, as a composition of three laws already there (Flow.stays_below_at, Flow.given_zero_below, Flow.uptake_needs_replenishment_from); no proof on main becomes a case of it, and landing it adds lines.

declarations.name: Becoming.ScratchReach.Needed definitions (barren, spring, doubling, tent, stay, atOnce, fall, oneAbove, atTake, always, never, Ahead, Cycle)
declarations.lean_statement:
def barren (_ : Nat) : Nat := 0
def spring (z : Nat) : Nat := 1 - z
def doubling (z : Nat) : Nat := z
def tent (z : Nat) : Nat := min z (4 - z)
def stay (x _ : Nat) : Nat := x
def atOnce (_ m : Nat) : Nat := m
def fall (x m : Nat) : Nat := if x < m then x + 1 else 0
def oneAbove (p : Nat × Nat) (_ : Nat) : Nat := p.1 + 1
def atTake (p : Nat × Nat) (_ : Nat) : Nat := p.1
def always (_ : Nat) : Bool := true
def never (_ : Nat) : Bool := false
def Ahead (p : (Nat × Nat) × Nat) : Prop :=
  p.1.1 ≤ p.2 ∧ p.2 ≤ p.1.1 + 1 ∧ p.1.1 + 1 + (p.1.1 + 1) ≤ p.1.2
def Cycle (p : (Nat × Nat) × Nat) : Prop :=
  p = ((0, 4), 0) ∨ p = ((0, 4), 1) ∨ p = ((1, 4), 1) ∨ p = ((0, 4), 2)
declarations.told_in_words: The four givings, three moves of the take, two readings and two schedules of the countermodels, and the two regions their courses stay in (Ahead: value at the take or one above, level at least twice one more than the take; Cycle: four configurations with level four). Each has a docstring; each is in the audit with an empty axiom report.

impl.differs_from_asked:
AI-written (Fable). Both statements hold; nothing asked turned out false. Where what is proved differs from the wording asked:

(i) The reach lemma is given in three forms. `reach` is the one asked (on `pair after left` for any `after`, so a way whose next way reads the level is covered). Under it are `reach_levels` (the same on any level X stepping by RegimeMargin.step under any uses D: the form Pace.paced can use without regrouping) and `step_takes_all` (one step, no hi: a use at least the level leaves nothing). `rising_takes_all_by_reach` has rising_takes_all's statement word for word. I also restated rising_meets_level (`rising_meets_level_by_within`), because the private takes_at_hi is shared with it and the line count cannot be judged without it.

(ii) Holds as asked (`set_above_ends`), and in all four orders: the level under the take as it stands or as moved, the value read before or after the step (`set_above_ends_moved_first`, `set_above_ends_read_after`; all three are cases of `set_above_takes_all`). So there is no countermodel for another order to keep.
- The conclusion is sharper than asked: `set_above_takes_all` names the step, hi*(L+1)+1. It equals (2*hi+1)*L at L = 1 and is below it for L of two or more (hi at least one). I did not prove that hi*(L+1)+1 is least or reached for L above one.
- Less is needed than asked. Of Regulation.Between only its two lower bounds are used (`low`: the take after a move is not below both the take and the value); the take may pass the value, or move away from it from above, and the stock still ends (also searched: 200,000 random courses under the weaker premises, 0 violations, /Users/ren/tmp/dj/batch17/reach-and-held-value/check_weaker.py; a search, not a proof). Strict nearing is needed only from below the value.
- "Strictly nearer when they differ" is stated as `raises : ∀ x m, x < m → x < A x m`, the form Regulation.Between.gap_falls already takes (its `raises`; its `lowers` is not asked). `raises_of_nearer` proves that a strictly falling gap wherever take and value differ gives it, so the gap wording is covered by composition, not as a premise of set_above_ends itself.
- The schedule premise is `gaps : ∀ t, ∃ r, t ≤ r ∧ r < t + L ∧ reads r = true` (every L steps in a row hold a reading step). It makes L at least one, which the bound uses.
- The argument is not the paper's. The paper counts readings (the take at reading k+1 is at least the lesser of the takes at readings k and k-1, plus one). I count steps: whatever the take and the value both are at least is kept by every turn, and is one more two steps after any reading step, so it is at least k at step k*(L+1). The reading-indexed inequality is not proved.
- (ii) rests on `reach_levels`, the level form of the reach lemma, not on the pair form `reach`: the regrouping of a paced course into the pair with an arbitrary reading (regroup_orbit) is private in TurningInTime and I did not re-prove it.

Not concluded anywhere: that the level stays nothing once it is; the ending as the end of a line under a need (TurningInTime.net); "a course that lasts has a reading that sets the value at or below the take" as a separate contrapositive statement.

The audit prints axioms for the 33 public declarations only; the 20 private lemmas are covered through the public theorems that use them.

read.is_it_a_link:
Neither a link between two atlas dynamics. Read against /Users/ren/theories/theories/becoming/results/atlas/entries/dynamics.json and the four conditions frozen in LINKS-ON-PAPER.md.

Section 1 (step_takes_all, levels_within, reach_levels, pair_within, reach) is a more general law inside one dynamic, `turning-in-time`, whose entry already lists TurningInTime.kept_within, rises_from, rising_takes_all and rising_meets_level. rising_takes_all becomes its case through rises_from; both ends are in that one dynamic. Its one-step part is already `LineOnAStock.step_zero`, a declaration of `a-line-on-a-stock`, which already names rising_takes_all and kept_within; landing it upstream would make those two dynamics share one lemma where they now hold two copies, and would add no new join.

Section 2 (set_above_rises, set_above_takes_all, the three set_above_ends) is a new law, a second case of reach_levels beside rising_takes_all. Its carrier is `Pace.paced`, and no atlas dynamic lists any Becoming.Pace declaration. It names definitions of other dynamics and no law of them: `RegimeMargin.step` is a declaration of `margin-of-a-regime` (FromNothing and Keeps are not atlas declarations), and neither ends_iff_below nor holds is used; `Regulation.Between` is not a declaration of `two-sided-regulation-and-late-reading`, `overshoot-beyond-the-gap` or `late-relay-oscillates`, and the proof only unfolds its two lower bounds (low_of_between) and uses the arithmetic lemma gap_of_ge. The laws it does use are TurningInTime.kept_within and Pace.stays_turned, Pace.paced_succ. Against the frozen conditions: condition 2 fails (`above` and `gaps` are premises neither side takes); condition 3 fails on the Regulation side (changing Between's upper bounds leaves the statement true, as set_above_takes_all itself proves); it is not a path between two dynamics. No old proof becomes a case of it, as the report says.

So: one generalisation within `turning-in-time` with an old law as its case and lines rising, and one new law that would be a new entry or an addition to `turning-in-time`. The map's link numbers would not change by a law that names laws of two dynamics.
